pages.title: Numbers 1 to 5: Single Digit Starters
bulletPoints: 1: One golden Sun shining bright in the clear sky.
2: Two eyes to see, two ears to hear, and two shoes on feet.
3: Three sides on a triangle, three wheels on a tricycle.
4: Four legs on a table, four paws on a puppy, four corners on a square.
5: Five little fingers on one hand, high five for learning!

pages.title: Numbers 6 to 10: Filling the Ten-Frame
bulletPoints: 6: Six legs on an ant, six spots on a ladybug.
7: Seven colors in a rainbow: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red.
8: Eight legs on an octopus, eight corners on a cube.
9: Nine bowling pins standing in a neat triangle.
10: Ten little toes, two full hands of fingers, a complete decade!

pages.title: The Power of 10: Bundles and Units
bulletPoints: 10 is special: It is the base of our entire decimal counting system.
Tying sticks: Tie ten single sticks together with a ribbon to make one bundle of 10.
Zero the hero: 10 has 1 ten and 0 ones.
Coins: 10 one-rupee coins stack up to equal one ten-rupee note!

pages.title: Teens 11 to 15: One Ten and More
bulletPoints: 11: Eleven = 1 ten + 1 one (10 + 1).
12: Twelve = 1 ten + 2 ones (10 + 2 = a dozen eggs!).
13: Thirteen = 1 ten + 3 ones (10 + 3).
14: Fourteen = 1 ten + 4 ones (10 + 4).
15: Fifteen = 1 ten + 5 ones (10 + 5 = 15 minutes is a quarter hour).

pages.title: Teens 16 to 20: Reaching Two Decades
bulletPoints: 16: Sixteen = 1 ten + 6 ones (10 + 6).
17: Seventeen = 1 ten + 7 ones (10 + 7).
18: Eighteen = 1 ten + 8 ones (10 + 8).
19: Nineteen = 1 ten + 9 ones (10 + 9).
20: Twenty = 2 full tens and 0 ones (10 + 10 = 20)!

pages.title: Place Value: Tens and Ones Columns
bulletPoints: In any 2-digit number, the left digit shows Tens and the right digit shows Ones.
In 23: The 2 stands for 20 (two bundles of 10) and the 3 stands for 3 singles.
In 28: 2 tens + 8 ones = 28.
Expand any number: 25 = 20 + 5. Simple, clear, and powerful!

pages.title: The Roaring Twenties: 21 to 25
bulletPoints: 21: Twenty-one = 2 tens and 1 one.
22: Twenty-two = 2 tens and 2 ones (twin twos).
23: Twenty-three = 2 tens and 3 ones.
24: Twenty-four = 2 tens and 4 ones (24 hours in a full day!).
25: Twenty-five = 2 tens and 5 ones (quarter of 100).

pages.title: Cruising Twenties: 26 to 30
bulletPoints: 26: Twenty-six = 26 letters in the English alphabet!
27: Twenty-seven = 3 x 3 x 3 cube number.
28: Twenty-eight = 28 days in the shortest month of February.
29: Twenty-nine = 2 tens and 9 ones.
30: Thirty = 3 complete tens and 0 ones (10 + 10 + 10 = 30)!

pages.title: Thrilling Thirties: 31 to 35
bulletPoints: 31: Thirty-one days in January, March, May, July, August, October, December.
32: Thirty-two teeth in an adult human mouth!
33: Thirty-three = 3 tens and 3 ones (double threes).
34: Thirty-four = 30 + 4.
35: Thirty-five = 7 groups of 5.

pages.title: High Thirties: 36 to 40
bulletPoints: 36: Thirty-six inches in one yard, 6 x 6 square.
37: Thirty-seven degrees Celsius = healthy human body temperature!
38: Thirty-eight = 30 + 8.
39: Thirty-nine = 1 less than forty.
40: Forty = 4 bundles of ten (10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40)!

pages.title: Fantastic Forties: 41 to 45
bulletPoints: 41: Forty-one = 4 tens and 1 one.
42: Forty-two = 6 groups of 7.
43: Forty-three = 40 + 3.
44: Forty-four = twin fours (4 tens and 4 ones).
45: Forty-five minutes in a half of a soccer match!

pages.title: Reaching Fifty: 46 to 50
bulletPoints: 46: Forty-six human chromosomes inside our cells.
47: Forty-seven = 4 tens and 7 ones.
48: Forty-eight hours in a two-day weekend.
49: Forty-nine = 7 x 7 square.
50: Fifty = 5 whole tens! Halfway to one hundred!

pages.title: Comparing Numbers: More, Less, and Equal
bulletPoints: Greater than (>): The hungry alligator mouth opens toward the bigger number (45 > 32).
Less than (<): The sharp point points to the smaller number (18 < 29).
Equal to (=): Both sides balance identically (25 = 20 + 5).
Rule: Compare the tens digit first! 41 has 4 tens; 39 has 3 tens; so 41 > 39.

pages.title: Forward & Backward Counting to 50
bulletPoints: Forward rocket launch: 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 50!
Backward countdown: 50, 49, 48, 47, 46, 45, 44...
Before and after: What comes right before 30? 29! What comes right after 49? 50!
Between numbers: The number between 38 and 40 is 39.

pages.title: Skip Counting by 2s up to 50
bulletPoints: Reaching fifty: 42, 44, 46, 48, 50!
Even number secret: All 2s skip numbers end only in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.

pages.title: Skip Counting by 5s up to 50
bulletPoints: Only 10 hops from start to 50!
Ten hands of fingers: 10 hands x 5 fingers = 50 fingers waving hello.
Clock minutes: The minute hand at 10 points to 50 minutes past the hour.

pages.title: Towers of 10 up to 50
bulletPoints: 10: One tower of ten.
20: Two towers of ten.
30: Three towers of ten.
40: Four towers of ten.
50: Five towers of ten.
Notice the pattern: The units place stays locked at 0 while tens increment 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

pages.title: Odd and Even Friends to 50
bulletPoints: Even numbers: Can be divided into pairs with zero left over (ends in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8).
Odd numbers: Always have one lonely friend left without a pair (ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, 9).
27 is odd because it ends in 7; 48 is even because it ends in 8.
Odd + Odd = Even (3 + 5 = 8); Even + Even = Even (4 + 6 = 10).

pages.title: Number Mazes: Finding Missing Numbers
bulletPoints: Puzzle 1: 22, 23, __, 25, 26. The missing number is 24!
Puzzle 2: 35, 40, __, 50. Skip counting by 5s reveals 45!
Puzzle 3: 50, 40, __, 20, 10. Counting down by 10s reveals 30!
Pattern detective: Look at the difference between neighbors to unlock any sequence.

pages.title: The Grand 1 to 50 Champion Certificate
bulletPoints: You have conquered all 50 numbers from one little drop of water to fifty ocean waves.
You understand tens and ones, greater than and less than, and skip counting tracks.
Math is everywhere: Counting steps, measuring heights, and sharing snacks fairly.
Wear your champion smile: You are a master of Numbers 1 to 50!
